svg.title: Page 3 — Reliability Gates and Tiers
svg.desc: Illustrated decision flow explaining confirmed historical precedent matching, Gate A chance testing, comparison of the two brains, and the complete T1 through T4 conditions.
svg.text: Check the evidence, then choose the tier
PAGE 3 · GATE B HISTORY · GATE A CHANCE TEST · T1–T4
START WITH BRAIN 1'S UPDATED LEADER
Brain 1 has applied its rules and any logged checks. Gate B evaluates the leader
before the critic comparison; Gate A evaluates the leader after Gate B.
GATE B · COMPARE WITH CONFIRMED PRECEDENTS
How the search works
1. Search confirmed cases only; exclude the current case.
2. Require the same dispenser class and material family.
3. Compare shared numeric photo signals; exclude signals at chance level.
4. Normalize each difference by that signal's spread across confirmed cases.
5. Keep mean normalized distance ≤1.0; return up to 10 closest matches.
This is numeric signal matching, not complaint-text search or embedding similarity.
Unconfirmed, plausible, and unverified cases are not Gate B precedents.
Decision 1: Are there at least 3 matches?
NO — fewer than 3
No ranking adjustment
YES — 3 or more
Check diagnosed matches
Decision 2: Do diagnosed matches contradict the leader?
Count only matches with a recorded diagnosis. If no more than half contradict, do not penalize.
If more than half contradict, subtract min(0.4, 0.4 × contradiction share) log-odds and re-rank.
History can lower a score; agreement never raises one. Normal T1 history requires ≥3 matches and zero diagnosed contradictions.
COMPARE THE TWO BRAINS
Compare Brain 2's clear top pick with Brain 1's top cause after Gate B.
Same cause → no disagreement · Different causes → clear disagreement
Critic abstains or is unavailable → no effective objection, not active agreement.
GATE A · IS THERE AN ABOVE-CHANCE DECIDING SIGNAL?
Gate A inspects the updated top cause's signal evidence and selects
the signal with the largest absolute rule contribution.
Only the small-dot-then-oversized-dot pattern can decide this gate.
Selected pattern + exact binomial p < 0.05 → ABOVE CHANCE.
p ≥ 0.05, another signal, or no signal evidence → NOT ABOVE CHANCE.
Other measurements can show a defect or unstable process, but do not identify its cause for Gate A.
TIER DECISION ORDER
FIRST — Do checks confirm exactly one cause, not also rule it out, and is it now #1?
YES → T1 immediately. This direct-check path takes priority over critic disagreement and the normal gates.
NO — Use critic disagreement and the Gate A / Gate B results as shown below.
T1 · STRONGEST
Either:
• Checks uniquely confirm
the current leader; OR
• No clear objection, Gate A
above chance, ≥3 matches,
zero diagnosed contradictions.
T2 · PROVISIONAL
No clear critic objection,
but the normal evidence
conditions for T1 are
incomplete and checks have
not uniquely confirmed the
current leader.
T3 · DISAGREEMENT
Critic has a clear, different
top cause AND Gate A is
above chance.
Keep the disagreement visible;
do not hide it or blend scores.
T4 · DO NOT FORCE
Critic has a clear, different
top cause AND Gate A is
not above chance.
Do not call one cause settled;
suggest a distinguishing check.
IMPORTANT DISTINCTION
A T1 ranking is not a case closed as CONFIRMED.
T1 describes support for the current ranking. CONFIRMED requires a separate repair verification.
NEXT → Page 4: what the operator sees, how checks re-rank, and how a repair is verified
